transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, I... I suppose I'm here because everyone just keeps acting like this whole foreclosure situation is just, you know, standard paperwork. Like it's just some routine thing about missed payments and late fees. But it's absolutely not. People keep trying to brush it off as this normal administrative process, but I know exactly what's actually going on. 

I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and... and even people at my job—which is just incredible to me, that the people I work with at the store would get involved in this—but they have all been quietly working together behind the scenes. It's all coordinated. They are all working together just to push me out of my house. And they think I don't see it, or that I'm just going to accept their little narrative. They keep sending these thick envelopes and waving all these official-looking legal documents in my face, but honestly, no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes. I've been watching them do this for almost two years now. Two whole years of them maneuvering and whispering behind my back to take my home, and everybody just wants to pretend it's just about a mortgage.
Do you believe that people are working against you or plotting to harm you in any other areas of your life, outside of the foreclosure situation?

No, no, it’s not like that at all. I mean, I don't walk around thinking the whole world is out to get me. If the house isn't involved, if we're just talking about my normal, everyday life... everything is completely fine. I get up every single morning, I make my coffee, I take care of myself, and I go to work. I supervise a whole team at the store, and they rely on me heavily. I'm the one who has to sit down and figure out all the shift schedules, which, let me tell you, is practically a full-time job on its own with people constantly calling out or needing shift swaps. And I handle all the difficult customer issues, too. If someone is throwing a fit at the register because a coupon expired three weeks ago, I’m the one who steps in, calms them down, and resolves it. I do my job, and I do it well. 

The issues... the only time things get complicated is when they try to cross those boundaries. It’s when the mail comes, those thick envelopes I mentioned, or when I get these incessant, vague calls from the bank while I'm trying to eat my lunch. Or—and this is what really gets to me—when I'm just trying to do my job at the store and suddenly there's some new workplace paperwork they want me to sign. They always frame it as some standard policy update or a routine form, but I can see right through it. I know exactly how it’s tied to what they are doing with the house. That is when the problems start, because I have to be so incredibly vigilant to catch what they're sneaking into my day. But if it has absolutely nothing to do with the property? No, no one is plotting against me. I'm just living my life, doing my schedules, managing my team... it's just that they won't leave the house out of it, you know? They just keep pushing it into my daily routine.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being taken out of your mind or broadcast to others?

What? No. No, that sounds... I mean, that sounds like something out of a science fiction movie, honestly. My thoughts are entirely my own, believe me. I have more than enough going on in my own head just trying to keep everything straight without anyone else putting things in there. I mean, think about it—between remembering which cashier needs Sunday off because of their childcare situation, and who is supposed to be covering the front registers during the lunch rush, and then, on top of all of that normal stuff, having to constantly, meticulously analyze every single piece of mail that the bank sends me to see what trap they've set this time... my mind is constantly running. It is always going. But it's *my* mind running. It's just me in there. 

Nobody is putting things in my head, and nobody is taking them out, either. Honestly, if they could just reach in and take my thoughts out, they would already know exactly how I'm planning to respond to their next fake legal notice, wouldn't they? They wouldn't have to keep sending people to the store with these supposed "updated employee agreements" to try and trip me up. They don't know what I'm thinking, which is exactly why they have to keep testing me. They are desperately trying to figure out what I know, because they absolutely cannot see inside my head or hear my thoughts. 

So, no, my thoughts are completely private. It's just me, thinking through every single detail, having to stay ten steps ahead so I don't miss a single trick they try to pull. I really don't know what you mean by thoughts being broadcasted or taken out. That's just... no, that's not happening at all. Everything in my head is mine.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that others could not understand or that turned out to be completely untrue?

No, not really. I mean, I don't just go around making things up or believing things that aren't real. I've always been a very grounded person. You have to be, in my line of work. When you're managing a whole team of retail workers, dealing with inventory discrepancies, and handling customer complaints all day, you don't have the luxury of living in a fantasy world. You deal with facts. You deal with what's right in front of you. 

So, no, I haven't had any... strange beliefs that turned out to be untrue. Everything I believe, everything I know is happening, is based on solid evidence. It's based on what I see with my own eyes, what I read in those letters, and how people act around me. Like I said before, I see the connections. I see how the bank's letters line up perfectly with the days my manager suddenly wants to have a "quick check-in" about my performance, or how the scheduling system at work suddenly glitches the exact same week I get a notice about a missed payment. These aren't just random coincidences, and they certainly aren't untrue suspicions. 

I know some people might not understand it at first glance. If you just looked at one letter, or just heard about one weird interaction at the store, you might think, "Oh, it's just a coincidence." And I get that. I really do. People who aren't in the middle of it don't have the full picture. They don't see the pattern. But when you live it every single day, when you have to meticulously document every piece of mail, every phone call, every strange look from a coworker... you realize that it's all connected. It's not a misunderstanding on my part. It's just that other people haven't done the work to connect the dots like I have. So, no, I haven't been wrong about these things. I've been incredibly, unfortunately right.

Because if you ask my family, or if you ask anyone at the bank, they certainly act like what I’m saying is strange or hard to believe. Honestly, that is the entire reason I’m even here talking to you right now. I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure situation is just... just standard paperwork and a few missed payments. They look at me, they tilt their heads, and they use that patronizing voice to say, "Oh, it's just a clerical issue," or "It's just standard bank procedure, you just fell behind."
